The cannon experiment has 13 usable rows out of 200; the other 187 are #DIV/0! from empty shot counts and must not be read as zero.

shipped_client_verdict.label: PROVED
shipped_client_verdict.how: MaterialManager MonoBehaviour PathID 1373 in level0 parsed byte-exact via UnityPy get_raw_data (6304/6304 bytes consumed, 0 remaining): 32 materials carrying ONLY name, id, ComponentMaterial enum {metal,wood,none,atlas}, tintColor, specColor, paintColorSets. No mass/density/durability/quality field. Swept all 8 game DLLs as BOTH UTF-8 and UTF-16LE string dumps (a plain 'grep -a' on .NET DLLs is a FALSE NEGATIVE - user strings are UTF-16LE); swept 55,885 MonoBehaviours / 1,247 distinct file x script pairs across level0, level1, resources.assets, sharedassets0/1. Asset bundles are island terrain only (255 x <id>@island_unityclient); all gameplay prefabs are in resources.assets. clientGameDB.bytes has no material table.
controls: 'Ship weighs more' -> Assembly-CSharp.dll (proves the UTF-16 dump sweep was live)
MonoScript name map resolved 5084/5084 from globalgamemanagers.assets
'baseHPValue = 2000f' found in the same decompiled tree where the tier factors 0.875/0.7777/0.7083 returned 0 hits
shipped_client_verdict.consequence: Mass and durability are SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE. The client is a display layer: ParentingMassAdderVisualizer assigns Rigidbody mass straight from component 1257, and CraftingStationClientState (1005) carries an already-computed float currentWeight plus predictedStats. All client users are Reader-only. The community spreadsheet numbers are therefore neither corroborated NOR contradicted by the shipped client - the client simply does not carry them, and they could only ever have lived on Bossa's dead server workers.
shipped_client_verdict.roster_note: The client still ships the REMOVED materials (platinum, palladium, magnesium, ebony, ironwood, mahogany, maple) as colour definitions. Still no pine.

rebalance_history.label: WIKI
rebalance_history.why_it_matters: Materials were rebalanced repeatedly, so a mass value without a patch date is not a fact about the game, only about a moment in it.

notes.verbatim: Wood weight reduced across the board by 15%.
To coincide with the re-implementation of overheat, ALL METAL STATS HAVE BEEN REBALANCED.
Iron, Lead, Bronze, Tin, Nickel, Alum, Eternium rebalanced.
Copper/Silver/Gold have had their weight reduced
Some woods have had their durability reduced

dating_analysis.label: DERIVED
dating_analysis.conclusion: UNRESOLVED - the evidence points both ways and is recorded rather than resolved.
dating_analysis.wood_signal: Beta 0.2.0.5's 'reduced across the board by 15%' predicts wiki = community x 0.85. Observed mean ratio across all 8 woods is 0.846, and the direction is right for all 8 - but per-material rounding only reproduces 4 of 8 exactly. Strongly suggestive, not conclusive.
dating_analysis.metal_signal_for_community_being_LATER: Update 31 says copper, silver and gold had their weight REDUCED. Community values are lower than wiki for exactly those three, three for three (0.55->0.50, 0.66->0.55, 0.73->0.69).
dating_analysis.metal_signal_for_community_being_EARLIER: The community sheets contain NO epilar, orthite or eternium, and those three metals were introduced in Update 29. A post-Update-31 sheet covering 12 metals would be expected to include them.
dating_analysis.counter_evidence: The wiki/community metal deltas do not run in one direction: nickel, lead and tungsten are HIGHER in the community table while aluminium, titanium, tin, iron and steel are lower and bronze is identical. That is not a single patch delta in either direction.
dating_analysis.wiki_table_dating: Metal.wikitext is tagged {{NeedsUpdate|page}}, includes epilar/orthite/eternium (so post-Update-29), yet still shows the pre-Update-31 higher copper/silver/gold weights. It is therefore most likely Update-29/30-era and NOT the final shutdown balance, contrary to how MaterialCatalog.cs describes it.

panel_resilience_is_flat.label: WIKI
panel_resilience_is_flat.finding: Panels.wikitext gives EVERY panel bar1value = 60 regardless of material, and Helms.wikitext 25. The wiki's own Resilience page says 'Only the casing affects resilience.' and carries no numbers at all - its data was an embedded Google Sheet that was never archived.
panel_resilience_is_flat.consequence: Supports the cannon-shot observation that a large panel takes 10-15 shots regardless of material: panel resilience may simply not have been per-material at that patch.

tungsten_resolution.label: DERIVED
tungsten_resolution.question: Tungsten is the single largest disagreement in the whole table.
tungsten_resolution.conclusion: THREE of the four sources cluster at 0.70-0.74 and the WAEngenius/panel value of 0.80 is the outlier. Two of those three are independent of each other: Falagar's 2017 guide (0.74) and my own fit to the wing-science raw kilogram readings (0.726-0.738, computed before the Falagar table was retrieved). That convergence is the strongest single piece of evidence in this investigation, because the wing fit reproduces every other metal within integer-rounding while missing tungsten by ~4 kg against the 0.80 value - and lands on Falagar's number instead. I would treat 0.80 as an error in the WAEngenius weight column, propagated into the panel sheet via the shared x40 table.

wood_mass_has_three_tiers.label: DERIVED
wood_mass_has_three_tiers.chain: Falagar 2017 / '03-Standard-WPU' tab (cedar 0.20) -> WAEngenius weight column (cedar 0.15) -> wiki (cedar 0.13)
wood_mass_has_three_tiers.note: Falagar 2017 and the 03-Standard-WPU tab agree within 0.01 on every wood, so they are ONE source, not two - which removes one of the four apparent wood tables. The remaining three are successive rebalances. Beta 0.2.0.5's 'Wood weight reduced across the board by 15%' fits the WAEngenius->wiki step in DIRECTION for all 8 woods (mean ratio 0.846 against a stated 0.85) but reproduces only 4 of 8 exactly under rounding, and does not explain the earlier Falagar->WAEngenius step (a uniform x0.75). Recorded, not resolved.
